rule: Each call in a multi-line method chain is reported on the line of its own method name, not the chain's first line. | **C7 Complete edges.** Caller and callee are never empty. The line is the line of the callee's name, per the ID-format rules. | Call on a receiver of **unknown type**: `recv.member`, using the LAST receiver segment (`self.client.get()` → `client.get`; `a.b.c()` → `b.c`). | Call on a **computed receiver** (call result, index, literal, `super` when the superclass is not in the scan): `.member` — a leading dot means "receiver unknown". | Not calls: passing a method reference (`x::m`, `self.m` without call), enum-variant/data construction (Rust `Some(x)`, `E::V(..)`, Haskell `Con {..}`), casts, language constructs (`isset`, `empty`, `sizeof`), declarations/function heads, module attributes, typespecs, field access without a call.
notes: The chain starts on line 6 (`return items`) but each call is on the line of its own method name (7, 8, 9). `.filter` is on `items` (unknown-type parameter) -> `items.filter`; `.map`/`.join` are on call results -> `.map`/`.join`. `isOk` on line 7 is passed, not called (no edge). `format` is declared after its use and resolves to `chain.format` (function declarations are top-level bindings, C1); the arrow folds into `chain.report`.
